clue.text: Rewritten, after resistance suppressed, it's antiracist, this guy figures?

indicators.note: something rewritten has had its words recast, so the letters left over are put into a new order
suppressed means held down and kept out, so the letter for resistance is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A man rewrites an antiracist slogan and wonders whether the numbers add up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressed' takes R out of IT'S ANTIRACIST, leaving ITSANTIACIST; 'Rewritten' rearranges those twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional who works with numerical data all day is literally a guy who figures.

clue.text: City flier's direction to avoid street

parts.note: a swan is a bird, a flier; with the possessive it gives the letters SWANS

indicators.note: to avoid means to steer clear of, so the street abbreviation is left out of the direction

parts.note: east is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A bird is told which way to fly so it stays clear of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a port city on the south coast of Wales.

clue.text: Article, easy to see, going over soldiers' food item

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: going over means covering or wrapping round, so the word for lit surrounds the soldiers

parts.note: something lit up is easy to see
men is a common crossword word for soldiers

explanation.surface: A clearly visible item gets passed around among the troops' rations.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is a formal word for nourishment or food.

clue.text: Home match — worried when Will's not available

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
a test is an international match, as in cricket
ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means worried

explanation.surface: Someone frets over a home fixture when their friend Will can't play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a man's name but is the legal document, a capital disguised by sitting first in a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Dying intestate means dying without having made a valid testament for one's estate.

clue.text: Duties ultimately — not requests

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the following word, not

parts.note: asks means requests, as a verb

explanation.surface: In the end these are obligations, not polite favours someone asks of you.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks are jobs or chores one is assigned, the same as duties.

clue.text: Calvin at intervals with partner — prevailing trend

indicators.note: at intervals tells the solver to take every other letter of Calvin, starting with the first

parts.note: a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: Calvin occasionally joins his partner in following the latest fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Climate in the figurative sense is the general mood or tendency of the times, such as a climate of opinion.

clue.text: Fruit bed after month not quite finished

indicators.note: after places the bed behind the shortened month
not quite finished means the month is cut off just before its final letter

parts.note: April is a month
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A fruit bed gets planted after a month of work that isn't quite done.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a small orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Absurd, our sprees — opt to change

indicators.note: to change asks for these letters to be altered into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Our wild binges are ridiculous, so we decide to mend our ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Preposterous is a stronger synonym of ridiculous, meaning contrary to reason.

clue.text: One's pragmatic about celebrities

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: Someone takes a hard-headed view of famous people.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who sees things as they are and acts practically is described as pragmatic.

clue.text: No way to have prepared drink for James in prison, Communist

definitions.text: No way to have prepared drink for James

parts.note: stir is slang for prison
red is a common word for a Communist

explanation.surface: Bond's martini is never made that way, says a Communist inmate.
explanation.walkthrough: James is James Bond, who famously wants his martini 'shaken, not stirred'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bond's catchphrase rules out mixing his drink with a spoon, so that method is no way to make it.

clue.text: The Italian, moving north, put in month at German city food shop

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the reversed article goes into the month

parts.note: DEC is the abbreviation for December

indicators.note: in a down clue, moving north means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: il is the Italian word for 'the'
Essen is a city in the Ruhr, western Germany

explanation.surface: An Italian heads north and sets up shop in a German city one month.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a shop selling prepared and imported foods.

clue.text: Have people to enforce law, sedulous, at borders

parts.note: a posse is a band of people summoned to enforce the law

indicators.note: at borders points to the outermost letters of sedulous, its first and last

explanation.surface: A sheriff's band of diligent helpers patrols the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to own or hold it, the same as having it.

clue.text: What might hobble horse, or dog when current's cold

indicators.note: when ... 's (is) says the current turns into cold, one letter standing in place of another

parts.note: a spaniel is a breed of dog
I is the physics symbol for electric current
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A tether for a horse or a dog when the stream runs cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current's' reads as 'current is', so the I in SPANIEL becomes C.
explanation.definitionFit: A spancel is a rope used to tie an animal's legs, especially a cow's or horse's, to stop it wandering.

clue.text: Examine temperature — not adequate

parts.note: to scan is to examine closely

explanation.surface: A doctor checks a patient's temperature and finds it lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means barely sufficient, so too little to suffice.

clue.text: Genuine gold article, not piece regularly seen

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
the is the definite article

indicators.note: regularly points to every other letter of the words not piece, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A real gold item, though no piece of it is often on show.
explanation.definitionFit: Authentic means real or of undisputed origin, as opposed to fake.

clue.text: Score at finish in such a position?

definitions.text: Score at finish in such a position?

parts.words: Score at finish in such a position?
parts.note: a score is twenty, so the item at the finish of a score stands in the matching ordinal place; the surface suggests a final scoreboard ranking

explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' reads as a sports result, but it is the number twenty; the last of twenty things holds that ordinal place.
explanation.definitionFit: The final member of a run of twenty occupies the ordinal place after nineteenth.

clue.text: Away in Europe on vacation, exotic Welsh ruler

indicators.note: in puts the scrambled Welsh and the ruler inside the emptied continent
on vacation means vacated, emptied, so only the outer letters of Europe remain
exotic means strange or foreign, so the letters of Welsh are rearranged

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, a queen

explanation.surface: A strange Welsh monarch is abroad somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Away' reads as part of the holiday scene but is the definition; 'in' then works as the container signal rather than a preposition of place.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsewhere means in another place, so not here, as in being away.

clue.text: On field one might insult winter traveller

definitions.meaning: in cricket, sledging is taunting a batsman on the field, and one who does it is so called
someone riding a sled over snow

explanation.walkthrough: Sledging is cricket slang for verbal abuse of an opponent during play; cricket is a bat-and-ball game popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the noun formed on sledge: a cricket taunter, or one who travels by sledge in snow.

clue.text: Our group getting over a call, tiresome

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting over puts one piece on top of the next

parts.note: we is the pronoun for our group
to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: Our team finds it exhausting to get past one more phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing means tiring or exhausting, as in a wearing day.

clue.text: Revolutionary path, centrepiece of work, was effective

indicators.note: centrepiece of takes the middle letters of the word work

parts.note: bit, as when brakes or a policy bit, means took effect

explanation.surface: A revolutionary's route through the heart of the job was successful.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is the circular path of a body going round another, a path of revolution.

clue.text: Work supporting old retreat, providing everything needed

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath what comes before

parts.note: a nest is a snug retreat
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A job propping up an old hideaway supplies all that is required.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-stop shop or service caters for all of a customer's requirements in a single place.

clue.text: Flatter by including NI port?

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the word by surrounds the port

parts.note: Larne is a port in Northern Ireland (NI)

explanation.surface: Can one sweet-talk someone by bringing a Northern Irish harbour into it?
explanation.walkthrough: Blarney is the Irish gift of the gab, named after Blarney Castle, so an Irish port fits the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: To blarney someone is to cajole them with smooth, flattering talk.

clue.text: Born too long ago — heading away from media reporting

indicators.note: heading away from means the first letter departs from the front of the media word

parts.note: coverage is the reporting of events by the media

explanation.surface: Someone too old for the job is leaving journalism.
explanation.definitionFit: Being over age means exceeding an age limit, having been born earlier than the cut-off.

clue.text: Dog ignores black bird

indicators.note: ignores means leaves out, so the letter for black is dropped from the dog

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of hound
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A dog takes no notice of a dark-feathered bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Race heats OK after review

indicators.note: after review means once revised and reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A racing official confirms the qualifying heats are fine once checked.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oaks is a flat horse race for fillies run each year at Epsom, south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oaks is the name of a famous English classic horse race.

clue.text: Player newly engaged by club, Leo for one is not good initially

parts.note: Leo is a star sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of is, not and good

explanation.surface: A club's new player is a Leo, which isn't a good start.
explanation.definitionFit: A new recruit to a sports team is called the club's latest acquisition under contract.

clue.text: Garden tent erected, keeping agreement

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the answer is held inside these words

explanation.surface: A garden tent is pitched, keeping the neighbours happy.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding between states, as in the Entente Cordiale.

clue.text: Time worker on vessel, extremely hazy about program, gets bellicose

parts.note: a rigger works on a ship's rigging

indicators.note: about means round, so the ends of hazy go round the program
extremely takes the extreme, outermost letters of hazy

parts.note: an app is a computer program

explanation.surface: A deckhand, vague about some software, becomes aggressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Trigger-happy describes someone too ready to use force or fight, which is warlike.
